title: EP-3 aircraft-return negotiation: six April 24–30, 2001 cables
scope: Six target cables acquired and completely read, not the complete 46-document State collection. No new scholarly reading. Original PDFs and extracted full texts remain outside Git.
acquisition: Public official State Department URLs observed in the preserved public catalogue. All six downloads returned HTTP 200 and validated as PDFs. No restricted-system access or authentication bypass.

catalogue_evidence.scope: Catalogue records for the six target IDs; not a full reading of all underlying documents.
Catalogue records for the six target IDs; not a full reading of all underlying documents.

source_dependence: All six new records are from one American diplomatic source family. One cable reproduces a Chinese non-paper and Xinhua statement, but this does not provide independent Chinese archival corroboration. Distinguish reported speech, reproduced text and embassy comment.

sources.title: CHINESE WILL AGREE TO DATES FOR ASSESSMENT TEAM VISIT
sources.creator: US Embassy Beijing
sources.release_status: Released in full; public State Department FOIA case F-2010-07070. Historical classification markings are preserved in the facsimile; the released document is stamped UNCLASSIFIED.
sources.reading_scope: Complete four-page cable, paragraphs 1–5 and embassy draft; all extracted text read. Physical page 2 also visually inspected.

key_locators.proposal_and_authority: Paragraphs 1–2, physical pages 1–2: US request for assessment before broader discussion; proposed Chinese dates and document.
key_locators.flyout: Paragraph 3, physical page 2: symbolic objection, not core issue; no consent.
key_locators.embassy_draft: Paragraph 5, physical pages 3–4: proposed inspection, end-May return and associated costs.

interpretation_limits: Embassy report of Zhou’s statements, not an original Chinese instruction.
Embassy draft is not an agreed text.
Commentary about Chinese urgency and the likely effect of a simple document is American assessment.

sources.title: INSTRUCTIONS ON EP-3 ASSESSMENT TEAM VISIT; JOINT TERMS OF REFERENCE
sources.creator: US Department of State
sources.release_status: Released in full; public State Department FOIA case F-2010-07070. Historical classification markings are preserved in the facsimile; the released document is stamped UNCLASSIFIED.
sources.reading_scope: Complete three-page Washington instruction, masthead, paragraphs 1–5, appended draft and signoff; all extracted text read. Physical pages 1–2 also visually inspected.

key_locators.approval: Physical page 1 masthead: approved by Deputy Secretary Richard L. Armitage; drafting and clearance entries.
key_locators.authority_and_limits: Paragraphs 3–4, physical pages 1–2: discussion authority, politically rather than legally binding, prohibited commitments, final Washington approval before signature.
key_locators.authorized_draft: Paragraph 5, physical pages 2–3: inspection, options, end-May target and directly associated costs less deliberate damage.

interpretation_limits: Authorizes discussion, not automatic signature.
Reproduced US draft is not a concluded bilateral agreement.
The instruction does not authorize China to fly out the aircraft or establish that China accepted any return method.
Powell signoff alone does not establish personal reading or approval separate from the explicit Armitage approval entry.

sources.title: AFM ZHOU SAYS U.S. DRAFT DOCUMENT DOES NOT ADDRESS PRC CONCERNS
sources.creator: US Embassy Beijing
sources.release_status: Released in full; public State Department FOIA case F-2010-07070. Historical classification markings are preserved in the facsimile; the released document is stamped UNCLASSIFIED.
sources.reading_scope: Complete three-page cable, paragraphs 1–5 and signoff; all extracted text read. Physical page 2 also visually inspected.

key_locators.Chinese_objection: Paragraphs 2–3, physical pages 1–2: responsibility, future incidents, broader document and explaining results.
key_locators.alternative: Paragraph 4, physical page 2: Prueher suggests separate statements; Zhou suggests factual record.
key_locators.American_inference: Paragraph 5, physical pages 2–3: inferred Chinese urgency and possible leverage.

interpretation_limits: Chinese statements are recorded by the American embassy.
Proposals are not accepted terms.
The embassy’s assessment that a Chinese end-May preference could give the US leverage is not proof of Chinese internal authority or a causal explanation of settlement.

sources.title: EP-3 RETURN: MFA "DISAPPOINTED" U.S. WILL NOT NEGOTIATE DOCUMENT
sources.creator: US Embassy Beijing
sources.release_status: Released in full; public State Department FOIA case F-2010-07070. Historical classification markings are preserved in the facsimile; the released document is stamped UNCLASSIFIED.
sources.reading_scope: Complete three-page cable, paragraphs 1–6 and signoff; all extracted text read. Physical page 2 also visually inspected.

key_locators.requested_document: Paragraph 2, physical pages 1–2: responsibility, expenses and prevention; embassy note distinguishes an earlier reported verbal reconnaissance request.
key_locators.consensus_claim: Paragraph 3, physical page 2: Zheng says a document would help Chinese internal consensus.
key_locators.American_limit_and_restatement: Paragraphs 4–5, physical page 2: authority limited to April 25 draft; Zheng says restate positions, not negotiate new formulations.

interpretation_limits: The internal-consensus explanation is Zheng’s statement as reported by US officials, not independently recovered Chinese deliberation.
The report’s reference line says STATE 3944; the preceding Beijing 3944 cable is separately acquired and identified by its actual header.
No eventual Chinese response or signed agreement is established by this cable.

sources.title: CHINA AGREES TO EP-3 ASSESSMENT TEAM
sources.creator: US Embassy Beijing
sources.release_status: Released in full; public State Department FOIA case F-2010-07070. Historical classification markings are preserved in the facsimile; the released document is stamped UNCLASSIFIED.
sources.reading_scope: Complete ten-page cable, paragraphs 1–12, American non-paper, Chinese non-paper, reproduced April 29 Xinhua release and signoff; all extracted text read. Physical pages 5, 8 and 9 also visually inspected.

key_locators.document_status: Paragraphs 2–3, physical page 2: China-only perspective and no response requested; embassy distinguishes its original intended joint document.
key_locators.access_publicity_target: Paragraphs 4–6, physical pages 2–3: assessment granted, publicity request, conditional end-May hope.
key_locators.initial_conditions: Paragraph 9, physical pages 4–7: five persons, two days, PLA control, objections and clarifications.
key_locators.no_flyout: Paragraph 9, physical pages 5–6: Lu repeats Zhou’s position that aircraft cannot be flown from Lingshui despite airworthiness checks.
key_locators.American_text: Paragraph 10, physical page 7: April 25 American draft reproduced.
key_locators.Chinese_text: Paragraph 11, physical pages 8–9: unilateral non-paper reproduces disagreement, payment discussion and inspection/return objectives.
key_locators.public_statement: Paragraph 12, physical pages 9–10: April 29 Xinhua text reproduced.

interpretation_limits: Cable date is April 30; the decisive meeting and Chinese paper are April 29.
The Chinese text is reproduced in a US diplomatic cable, not a separately acquired Chinese original or executed bilateral instrument.
Chinese paper calls its contents agreements, but the surrounding report expressly distinguishes its unilateral standing.
Conditional end-May hope is not completed return or guaranteed deadline.
Inspection and airworthiness checks do not establish permission to repair or fly out.
Embassy comments about compensation, domestic audience and Chinese willingness are assessments, not Chinese internal records.

sources.title: EP-3 ASSESSMENT TEAM: WORKING THE DETAILS
sources.creator: US Embassy Beijing
sources.release_status: Released in full; public State Department FOIA case F-2010-07070. Historical classification markings are preserved in the facsimile; the released document is stamped UNCLASSIFIED.
sources.reading_scope: Complete seven-page cable, paragraphs 1–6, all original conditions and updates, and signoff; all extracted text read. Physical pages 2, 4 and 5 also visually inspected.

key_locators.time_boundary: Paragraph 2, physical page 2: state of play current at 19:00 April 30 Beijing time.
key_locators.accepted_accommodations: Paragraph 3, physical pages 2–3: accompanying defense attaché officer, working days decided at airfield, direct team transport to Haikou.
key_locators.no_flyout_and_assessment: Paragraph 3, physical page 4: no equipment removal, checks for airworthiness, explicit no-flyout permission.
key_locators.power_sequence: Paragraph 4, physical page 5: objection and initial local flexibility, static-only prohibition, US clarification that engines would not run, renewed local discussion, senior MFA admission of technical uncertainty and PLA officers in Haikou; cart rental conditional on future approval.
key_locators.visa_and_local_staff: Paragraphs 5–6, physical pages 6–7: visas on arrival, local arrangements and embassy assessment of remaining risks.

interpretation_limits: Direct flight permission concerns the team’s chartered aircraft, not the EP-3.
No completed approval to power up is reported.
The senior MFA official is unnamed; the cable does not disclose internal mandate or identify authority to reverse the no-flyout position.
The reported technical uncertainty does not demonstrate that all restrictions or delays were accidental, or prove deliberate obstruction.
The April 30 state of play cannot exclude later changes in May.
